title: Highest temperature in London on September 1?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 1 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from sources like GFS and regional European guidance indicate a maximum temperature in Paris on September 1, 2026, likely peaking between 23–25°C under partly to mostly cloudy skies with light westerly to northwesterly winds around 5–10 km/h.** 

This setup limits strong diurnal heating from solar radiation while allowing modest advection of milder air, producing afternoon highs close to the early-September climatological average. The tight clustering of market-implied probabilities around 23°C and 24°C reflects model consensus on peak values, with minor spreads arising from differences in simulated cloud timing, boundary-layer mixing, and urban heat retention. Updated runs closer to the event will refine whether the thermometer registers nearer the lower or upper end of that narrow range, as small changes in insolation or wind can shift the daily maximum by 1°C.

**Forecast models and official guidance point to a maximum temperature of 31–32 °C in Shanghai on September 1, 2026, consistent with the market’s heavy weighting toward those outcomes.** 

Current conditions on August 31 show highs of 32–34 °C under partly cloudy skies with scattered showers possible. For September 1, guidance from multiple sources converges on a daytime high near 31 °C (some runs reach 32–33 °C early in the day before cloud cover and light rain develop), with overnight lows around 25–27 °C and easterly winds of 3–5 m/s. Humidity remains elevated (70–90 %), supporting heat indices near observed air temperatures but limiting further warming. 

The shift from recent peak summer values reflects seasonal cooling in the western Pacific subtropical high and increasing moisture from approaching frontal activity, which favors afternoon convection that caps daytime maxima. Model consensus places the highest probability on 31 °C, with modest upside risk to 32 °C if early-day clearing persists; probabilities drop sharply below 30 °C or above 33 °C given the narrow range of ensemble solutions. Updated short-range guidance and real-time observations on September 1 will be the key drivers of any final adjustment in market-implied odds.

Updated short-range model runs and local observations from Central Park will refine the exact maximum ahead of market resolution.
